nodes.title: Load Image  ->  feeds STAGE 1.5 and STAGE 2

widgets_values: One raven alone, the only subject in an empty frame. Full body side view, standing upright, wings folded tight against the body, head in profile with the beak pointing toward the right edge of the frame. The whole bird reads as one clean closed shape with an unbroken outline, every limb and feather tip clearly separated from the background. Even diffuse light from the upper left, gentle modelling across the body, the outline crisp and hard on all sides. The bird floats free against a seamless mid-grey studio backdrop that holds one even tone across the entire frame, empty above and below it. Generous margin on all four sides. Tack sharp.

A sunken relief carved into a flat walnut panel. The panel surface stays flat and untouched as the top plane, and the raven is cut down into it, its outline a sharp vertical step dropping below that surface. Inside the recess the bird is modelled in shallow rounded relief, the highest points of the back and head rising to sit flush with the panel face. Egyptian sunk relief carving. Broad simple confident planes, each feather group a single soft swell rather than fine texture. Matte unpolished wood. Raking light from the upper left throws one hard shadow along the inside of the cut outline and soft gradients across the modelled forms within. Keep the exact pose, silhouette and proportions. The background is the flat uncarved panel surface, one uniform tone, edge to edge.

Keep the raven exactly as it is: same pose, same silhouette, same proportions, same feather detail. Change only the presentation. The background becomes one completely flat even mid-grey tone across the whole frame. The bird stands alone on that empty flat field with nothing beneath it and nothing behind it. The outline is crisp, hard and unbroken all the way around, every toe and feather tip cleanly separated from the background. Even lighting across the body so the silhouette reads without ambiguity.

# Create Sunken Relief

Same four stages as `Create_Relief_Image`, plus a silhouette stage. **Every stage reads a FILE**, so an approved image is frozen on disk and cannot drift.

## Sunken is not inverted
A sunken relief is **not** a flipped bas-relief. The bird's modelling keeps its normal sense - the beak still stands proud of the eye socket. What changes is that the whole figure sits **below** the panel face, with a step cut down around its outline. Inverting a height map gives you a *mold*, where the beak is the deepest point. Do not invert anything here.

## The one node that matters
**Load Image** (teal, left) feeds BOTH Stage 1.5 and Stage 2. Whichever file you point it at is your position in the chain.

## STAGE 1 - generate candidates  (active)
Lighting is deliberately flatter than the bas-relief workflow. For sunken relief the **outline is the artwork** - it becomes a real cut line - so an unambiguous silhouette matters more than dramatic shadow. A deep cast shadow across the flank makes the outline unreadable and cannot be fixed downstream.

## STAGE 1.5 - cleanup  (muted)
Flattens the background and hardens the outline. Point Load Image at your saved Stage 1 file first.

## STAGE 2 - convert to SUNKEN relief  (muted)
Prompt asks for broad confident planes, not fine texture. The recess is only ~4 mm deep, so detail tuned for a 7 mm bas-relief turns to mush when compressed into it.

## STAGE 3 - depth map  (muted)
Unchanged. DA3 does not know or care whether the result will be raised or sunk.

## STAGE 4 - silhouette  (muted)  <- NEW
Turns the depth map into a clean black/white outline mask.

1. Run with Stage 3. Look at **STAGE 4 PREVIEW**.
2. Tune **THRESHOLD** until the bird is solid white on solid black with no holes and no background speckle.
3. **Grow / shrink** nudges the outline in or out by whole pixels.
4. **Close pinholes** fills small interior gaps. Raise kernel_size if holes remain.
5. Name it in **Save STAGE 4 silhouette**, Ctrl+M, Run, Ctrl+M off.

This mask defines the cut line, so it is worth more attention here than it was for the bas-relief. Toes and beak tip are where it usually breaks.

## Then what
The sunken height field itself is built in **Python**, not here. This workflow hands off two files: the **Stage 3 depth map** and the **Stage 4 silhouette**.
